title: Battle campsite named UK's most unique in 2026 awards
text:
Beech Estate Campsite in Battle has been named the most unique site in the UK at the 2026 Campsites.co.uk Camping and Glamping Awards.

The site is set within 600 acres of woodland on a private 2,000-acre estate, offering an off-grid experience with bell tents and hammocks. It has earned a 4.81-star rating, with 96 per cent of guests saying they would recommend it.

Beech Estate said its combination of secluded woodland pitches, traditional campfires, and warm bucket showers made it stand out. Hale Farm Campsite in Chiddingly also took runner-up spots for Best Campsite and Best Family Campsite in South East England.

title: Man arrested after car hits three people in Catsfield
text:
A 72-year-old man has been arrested following a serious collision between a car and three pedestrians in Catsfield. The incident occurred on The Stream at approximately 8.30am on Wednesday, 25 November.

Sussex Police said the man was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving and driving while unfit through drink or drugs. He remains in custody. Two children and a man were taken to hospital for treatment.

The road remains closed at the junctions with Church Road and near Watermill Stream. Police said enquiries remain ongoing.

title: A26 Eridge bridge inspected; Burwash wall repaired
text:
East Sussex Highways has completed principal inspections of the A26 bridge over the railway at Eridge. The work required special closures of the railway line, arranged through Network Rail, to allow inspectors to access the structure safely.

A lorry fitted with a special platform was used to examine the bridge while traffic lights controlled passing vehicles. This method allowed the team to get a close-up view of the structural elements to prepare a detailed condition report.

In Burwash, the team also repaired cracks in the parapet wall above the river on Willingford Lane. They used crack stitching, which involves cutting slots between bricks and fixing reinforcing bars with specialist grout to strengthen the wall without removing good brickwork.

title: Ombudsman upholds complaint against East Sussex Council over SEN plan
text:
The Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman has upheld a complaint against East Sussex County Council regarding the handling of a child’s Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plan. The decision, issued on 13 October 2026, found fault in how the council managed the case between February 2025 and March 2026.

The Ombudsman found that the council fettered its discretion by rigidly applying a policy that prevents amending an EHC Plan within 12 months of a Tribunal decision. It failed to properly consider information from a plan review and did not adequately assess its duty to provide alternative educational provision in early 2026. This approach caused distress and uncertainty for the family.

The council has agreed to apologise to the parent and make a symbolic payment. It will also review its policy to ensure it fully considers information gathered during plan reviews. The Ombudsman will share this decision with Ofsted.

title: New cancer support hub to open at Eastbourne DGH
text:
A new dedicated cancer support hub is arriving at Eastbourne District General Hospital. The facility will provide information, practical guidance, and emotional support for patients and families across East Sussex.

East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust said the hub was made possible by a £200,000 grant from Macmillan Cancer Support, which funded the entire project. The bespoke building was constructed off-site in Lancashire and is due to be delivered to the hospital on Saturday 28 November.

The hub will offer signposting, social prescribing, and a private counselling room for cancer teams. It is designed to give patients and families a space to talk away from busy clinical areas, supporting them from diagnosis through to end-of-life care.

title: Bexhill Christmas Light Switch-On set for 5 December
text:
Bexhill-on-Sea’s Christmas Light Switch-On and Christmas Market is scheduled for Saturday, 5 December. The event will take place on Western Road and Devonshire Square, running from 3pm until 7pm.

According to Bexhill-on-Sea Town Council, the celebration is held in association with the Bexhill Lions Club. The day begins at 3pm with an opening address from The Town Crier, who will also announce the winner of the Christmas Window Competition.

The main ceremony, featuring the Mayor of Bexhill-on-Sea and the Christmas Town Cry, is set for 5:30pm. The council noted that a full line-up of musical and theatrical acts will be announced soon.

title: Bexhill and Battle MP speaks on Civil Service Pension Scheme in Parliament
text:
Dr Kieran Mullan, the Conservative MP for Bexhill and Battle, spoke in the House of Commons on Tuesday 24 November regarding the Civil Service Pension Scheme.

Speaking in the chamber, he stated that several of his constituents, including Karen Allum and Janette Woolgar, face several months of delays in their payments. He asked the Minister what deadline has been set for Capita to resolve the issue and meet reasonable service standards.

The MP also voted on the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, voting against a motion to disagree with a Lords amendment, which passed 260 to 98. He voted in favour of an amendment to the same bill, which was defeated 93 to 278. He voted No on a related Armed Forces Bill motion.

title: On this day 1833: The cricketing priest who played for Cambridge in 1855
text:
John Sumner Gibson was born on 25 November 1833 in Chester. He was an English priest and a first-class cricketer, though his sporting career was brief. His single recorded first-class match was the 1855 University Match against Oxford, playing for Cambridge University. In that game, he batted low in the order, scoring 8 and 23, and did not bowl.

Gibson was the eldest son of William Gibson, a priest, and Eliza Maria, daughter of John Bird Sumner, Archbishop of Canterbury. The reformer and churchman William Wilberforce was also a relation. After Eliza Maria died in 1836, William Gibson married her cousin, Louisiana, daughter of Charles Sumner, Bishop of Winchester. Many of the thirteen children from these marriages carried 'Sumner' in their forenames, though John Sumner Gibson did not hyphenate his surname.

Educated at Harrow School and Trinity College, Cambridge, Gibson later served as a Church of England priest in Kent, Warwickshire, and Derbyshire until 1873. He then retired to East Sussex, dying in 1892 at Iridge Place, a listed country house near Hurst Green.

title: Battle care home hosts Tommy Tea Party for veterans
text:
Hazel Lodge Care Home in Battle hosted a Tommy Tea Party to raise funds for the Royal British Veterans Enterprise charity.

The event brought together residents, relatives, staff, and local veterans, alongside volunteers from The Battle Poppy Appeal and members of the local charity Veterans Growth.

Guests enjoyed an afternoon tea with live music from singer Laura, who performed wartime classics, followed by a quiz where the Battle Poppy Volunteers took the prize.

Rikki-Gene Bury, General Manager at Hazel Lodge, said the event was a "huge amount of fun" and that the community had been supportive of the cause.

title: Hundreds attend St Richard's fourth annual Christmas Fayre in Bexhill
text:
St Richard's Catholic College in Bexhill hosted its annual Christmas Fayre on Saturday, 21 November, with hundreds of people attending the event.

The day, now in its fourth year, was organised by the Parent, Teacher, and Friends Association (PTFA) and featured more than 40 independent stallholders, festive food and drinks, and entertainment.

Helen Dorling, PTFA chair, said the event started as an alternative to an outdoor summer fayre due to unpredictable weather. She noted that the gathering has grown each year, raising money for the school while fostering a sense of community spirit that she feels is increasingly rare.

title: Russell Brand effigy burned at Robertsbridge bonfire night
text:
An effigy of comedian Russell Brand was set alight during the bonfire celebrations in Robertsbridge on Saturday, November 21. The event saw the village’s Station Road and High Street described as a "river of fire" as the procession moved through the streets.

The torchlit march began at the station at 7.15pm, led by the Robertsbridge Society in costumes of monks and Roman centurions. The group made its way to the Recreation Ground, where a giant bonfire was lit, followed by a fireworks display.

Robertsbridge is known for its impressive bonfire effigies, with last year’s event targeting Prince Andrew after he was stripped of his royal title. The society has already launched a fundraiser for the 2027 event, asking for donations to help make next year’s celebration bigger and better.

title: Little Common come from behind to beat Pagham 4-1
text:
Little Common secured a 4-1 victory over Pagham at the Recreation Ground on Saturday, securing three much-needed points in the SCFL Premier.

The hosts fell behind in the 10th minute after failing to clear a free kick, but responded with a spectacular strike from Ollie MacDonald in the 23rd minute to level the score. Kieran Ludlow added a header before the break, while Freddie Warren and Sonny Tyrell scored in the second half to complete the turnaround.

Manager Russ Eldridge said the team showed "great character" to respond to the early deficit. He noted that while the early goal was disappointing, the squad's attitude and work rate were key to the win.

title: Battle Abbey Nursery visits Southlands care home for 104th birthday
text:
Children from Battle Abbey Nursery in Bexhill recently visited Southlands care home to celebrate a resident’s 104th birthday. The preschool group, known as the Oaks, created a card featuring 104 balloons made from their fingerprints and performed a rendition of Happy Birthday.

According to the nursery, the resident was seated in a throne with a glass of Ribena, surrounded by gold decorations. The visit was described as a moment that brought generations together in a joyful celebration.

title: Severe Weather Emergency Protocol active in Rother until Friday
text:
Rother District Council has activated its Severe Weather Emergency Protocol (SWEP) in response to current and forecasted weather conditions. The protocol is a locally agreed procedure designed to minimise the risk of harm to people sleeping rough by providing emergency accommodation.

The council stated that SWEP will remain active until Friday, 27 November. It is an offer for rough sleepers in Rother who do not have access to accommodation and require assistance during severe weather.

Those needing help should approach the council at the Town Hall on London Road, Bexhill on Sea, during office hours. If unable to attend in person, residents can call 01424 787000 during office hours or 0330 123 3517 for out-of-hours assistance.

title: De La Warr Pavilion staircase windows removed for heritage repair
text:
The distinctive staircase windows at Bexhill’s De La Warr Pavilion have been removed as major internal refurbishment work begins. Scaffolding and security fencing are now in place around the area, with the curved glass and metal frames taken down for specialist restoration.

A spokesperson for the pavilion said the work is part of the “An Icon For Everyone” project, a partnership with Rother District Council and Haworth Tompkins architects. They explained that the north and south staircases are in disrepair, with cracks in the glass expanding during storms and signs of corrosion on the original single-glazed windows.

Specialist heritage contractor Associated Steel Window Services is handling the repairs. The windows have been transported to a workshop in Surrey for restoration, which includes installing new steel ring beams, curved metal beading, and new glazing to improve the building’s airtightness and long-term resilience.

title: County leader criticises government reorganisation plan
text:
East Sussex County Council has responded to the Government's call for further evidence on local government reorganisation. Cllr Andy Woolley, the council leader, stated that the Government has not explained the reasons for its proposal to create a new unitary authority for East Sussex, excluding East Saltdean, Peacehaven and Telscombe.

The council leader said the plan would transfer 26,000 people to Brighton and Hove without evidence that this benefits residents. He noted that the Government appears to be ignoring feedback from local residents who have raised concerns and rejected the plan. The council argued that breaking apart established public services, including social care, would be complex, costly and could put vulnerable residents at risk.

The council said it will resubmit its evidence during the current representation period. It hopes the Government will reconsider its decision, which it described as piling costs onto local people who are already struggling.

title: Council extends loan for Blackfriars housing scheme to 2029
text:
Rother District Council has agreed to extend the Development Facility Agreement for its housing company until 31 July 2029. The decision was made by the Shareholder Executive Committee on 18 November at the Town Hall in Bexhill-on-Sea.

The extension provides flexibility for the Blackfriars programme, where final completions are now expected in May 2029. Officers recommended the change to allow scope for any further delays without causing issues with the transfer of homes.

The council’s financial exposure on the project reached a peak of £38.6m in October 2026, against a total loan facility of £40m. While 130 homes were pre-sold to Places for People, the sale of the remaining 70 open market dwellings has been slower than anticipated due to weak market conditions and higher borrowing costs.

title: Jazz guitarist Nigel Price to play Bexhill's Blue Note
text:
Award-winning jazz guitarist Nigel Price is set to make his first appearance at the Blue Note Jazz Club in Bexhill on Sunday 6 December.

John Fordham of The Guardian noted, "Wes Montgomery guitar fans need look no further than the Uk's Nigel Price." His jazz career spans more than 30 years and he has performed more than 600 times at London’s Ronnie Scott’s Jazz Club. He has played on over 70 albums, including 12 as a leader.

Price will be joined by Mark Fletcher, the house drummer at Ronnie Scott’s for more than 20 years, and Nigel Thomas on double bass, a staple of the Brighton jazz scene for over 35 years. Lynda Murray, a saxophonist, will host the afternoon session.

The event is scheduled from 3pm to 5pm at the club on London Road, near the town hall. Tickets cost £15, payable by cash or card on the door, with the bar opening at 2.30pm.

title: Crowhurst Park Lodges wins Hoseasons guest satisfaction award
text:
Crowhurst Park Lodges in Battle has been named the Relax & Explore Small Park destination in the South of England at Hoseasons’ 21st annual Diamond Awards.

The awards recognise UK holiday parks, lodge resorts and boating locations rated highest by guests during the 2026 season. The ceremony took place at Celtic Manor Resort in Newport, South Wales.

A spokesperson for the park said the team always goes above and beyond to ensure guests have a fantastic break. Lloyd Sceats-Page, account director at Hoseasons, described the team as richly deserving winners who consistently go the extra mile to delight guests.

title: Bexhill beat Midhurst 5-1 to climb to sixth
text:
Bexhill put five past Midhurst and Easebourne in the latest in a long run of Polegrove fixtures which has seen the Pirates move steadily up the table. The win continues a strong run of form for the Pirates, who have been climbing steadily since September.

According to the Hastings Observer, Bexhill started brightly with Charlie Playford scoring in the first minute and Ash Latuske setting up Shonk for the second. Just before the break, Latuske lashed in a drive that had the keeper beaten all ends up but the ball somehow bounced back out into play off the inside of the post.

Midhurst pulled one back early in the second half, but Bexhill responded with goals from Theo Coombs and Shonk. Substitute Jack Samways added a fifth goal with a half-volley in the 76th minute, sealing the result.

title: Political accountability: Dollimore backs Visitor Levy and Immigration Bill in Commons
text:
Helena Dollimore, the Labour (Co-op) MP for Hastings and Rye, voted in favour of the Visitor Levy (England) Bill Second Reading on Monday 16 November. The bill passed with 296 votes to 96.

Dollimore participated in all 10 recorded votes this week, missing none. She did not vote against her party's position on any occasion. Her voting record included supporting the Immigration and Asylum Bill at its Third Reading on Tuesday 17 November, which passed 290 to 94. On the same day, she voted against four new clauses proposed during the Report Stage of the same bill. These clauses were defeated, with results ranging from 44 to 368 against to 60 to 410 against.

The MP is a member of the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Committee, the Statutory Instruments (Joint Committee), and the Statutory Instruments (Select Committee). She belongs to the Labour (Co-op) party.

Dollimore did not make any spoken contributions in the Commons nor table any written questions this week. However, she received three answers to questions she had previously tabled. On Monday, the Department for Transport responded to a query regarding the expansion of disabled persons railcard eligibility criteria, stating it aims to make rail travel more affordable. On Tuesday, the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs answered two questions. One addressed the government's stance on genetically modifying chickens to reach slaughter weight faster, noting support for voluntary moves away from fast-growing breeds. The other concerned steps to rewild natural landscapes to protect against extreme weather, with the department citing the Land Use Framework.

The Commons was sitting throughout the week, with votes recorded on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday.

title: Political accountability: MP raises Beckley school PE funding concerns in Commons
text:
Dr Kieran Mullan, the Conservative MP for Bexhill and Battle, raised a local issue in the Commons on Monday 16 November. He spoke during Topical Questions about the impact of government reforms on physical education funding at Beckley Church of England primary school. He stated that teachers and parents reported a "massive drop" in provision and asked the Minister to agree to meet him to discuss the situation in Beckley and other schools.

The MP participated in 8 of the 10 recorded Commons votes this week. He did not vote on the Immigration and Asylum Bill Third Reading or the Government Amendment on the Rosebank oil field. He voted against the Visitor Levy (England) Bill, which passed 296 to 96. He also voted against several new clauses in the Immigration and Asylum Bill Report Stage, all of which were defeated. He voted in favour of the Opposition motion on the Rosebank oilfield and the UK-EU relations debate, both of which were defeated. He voted against the Draft Employment Rights Act regulations, which passed 299 to 159. He voted against his party's position 0 times.

Dr Mullan serves as the Shadow Minister for Justice. He is a member of the Conservative Party.

The MP made six spoken contributions. On Tuesday 17 November, he asked the Minister to meet him and the MP for Bishop Auckland to discuss using a North Sea wealth fund for deep geothermal projects. On Wednesday 18 November, he spoke in debates on the Rosebank oilfield and UK-EU relations. He asked what percentage contribution Rosebank would make to global warming and questioned the security risks of relying on China for critical minerals. He also received three written answers. The Ministry of Defence stated it had not held discussions with Wealden District Council about cadet facilities at Crowborough Training Camp. The Home Office said it engages regularly with the Council regarding the camp's use. The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero confirmed it is accelerating low carbon technologies, including geothermal.

title: Political accountability: East Sussex County Council, week from Sunday 15 November to Saturday 21 November 2026
places: Bexhill, Battle, Rye, Rother villages, East Sussex
text:
East Sussex County Council confirmed decisions on transport and adult social care this week. The Lead Member for Transport and Environment noted decisions made on 20 July 2026 regarding the Pan-Sussex Minerals and Waste Plan Proposal and the Highway Vegetation Management Policy review. The Lead Member for Adult Social Care and Health confirmed decisions on residential and nursing provider payments, the Integrated Health and Wellbeing Service contract, and Disability Related Expenditure.

Six meetings were held this week. The Lead Member for Transport and Environment meeting on 16 November had one Reform UK councillor present. The SBSA Audit and Governance Committee on 17 November had eight councillors present and one apology. The Lead Member for Adult Social Care and Health meeting on 19 November had one Reform UK councillor present. The County Consultative Committee, Discretionary Transport Appeal Panel, and East Sussex Schools Forum also met, with no attendance figures recorded in the minutes for the latter three.

The council has 50 councillors. Reform UK holds 20 seats, the Liberal Democrats 14, the Green Party 10, the Conservatives 4, and Independents 2. Andy Woolley (Reform UK) is Leader of the Council. Kathryn Field (Liberal Democrats) leads the Liberal Democrat Group. Julia Hilton (Green Party) leads the Green Party Group. Paul Redstone (Conservative) leads the Conservative Group.

The SBSA Audit and Governance Committee discussed the appointment of a Chair and Vice-Chair, and received an introduction from Grant Thornton regarding external audit. They also reviewed the internal audit strategy and the approach to the Treasury Management Policy for 2027/28. Johnny Denis (Green Party) declared an interest as the Lewes District Council Cabinet member for community wellbeing, arts, culture, tourism and leisure, stating he did not consider it prejudicial.

In the next fortnight, the People Scrutiny Committee will meet on 23 November to discuss the Safeguarding Children Partnership Annual Report and the Crisis and Resilience Fund. The East Sussex Health and Wellbeing Board meets on 24 November to review the Health and Social Care Integration Programme and the response to the National Plan to End Homelessness. The Pension Committee meets on 26 November to review the Pension Board Minutes and the LGPS Governance. The Audit Committee meets on 27 November to review the Internal Audit Progress Report and the Auditor's Annual Report. The Place Scrutiny Committee meets on 30 November to review the Strategic Asset Plan and the Queensway Gateway Road post-project appraisal. Full Council meets on 1 December.

title: Political accountability: Battle boarding house licence approved despite objections
text:
A licensing panel has approved a Premises Licence for Battle Abbey School Boarding House on Whatlington Road. The licence covers alcohol sales, late night refreshment, and regulated entertainment, primarily for weddings and functions during school holidays. Hours are set from 12:00 to 00:30, Monday to Sunday. A report to the committee notes that eight representations objected to the application, citing concerns about crime, public nuisance, safety, and child protection. The officer recommendation was to determine the application, and the panel approved it.

Three meetings were held this week. At the Licensing and General Purposes Committee on 16 November, Tony Biggs (Conservative) and Polly Gray (Green Party) attended. Jimmy Stanger (Conservative) sent apologies. At the Overview and Scrutiny Committee on 16 November, nine councillors attended: four Conservatives, two Liberal Democrats, one Labour, one Green, and one Rother Association of Independent Councillors. Apologies were received from Charles Clark (Independent), Sam Coleman (Labour), and Kathryn Field (Liberal Democrats). The Shareholder Executive Committee met on 18 November with eight attendees: three Rother Association of Independent Councillors, two Labour, two Liberal Democrats, and one Green. Apologies were sent by Teresa Killeen (Liberal Democrats) and Ruairi McCourt (Labour).

The council has 38 councillors. The Conservative group has 13 members, led by Carl Maynard. The Liberal Democrats have 8, led by Susan Prochak. Labour has 6, led by Gareth Delany. The Rother Association of Independent Councillors has 6, led by Doug Oliver. The Green Party has 3, led by Polly Gray. Two independents serve on the council. Cabinet members include Doug Oliver (Leader), Susan Prochak (Deputy Leader), and others from various parties.

The Overview and Scrutiny Committee reviewed the second quarter performance report. A report to the committee says net direct emissions rose 40% to 51.61 TCO2e, exceeding the target. Housing performance was described as excellent, with an 80% increase in households prevented from homelessness. The committee also reviewed the budget, which forecasts a revenue surplus of £668,000. Capital works at the De La Warr Pavilion are delayed to March 2027, and Skinners Shed faces delays due to asbestos. The Shareholder Executive Committee reviewed the financial position of the Rother DC Housing Company. A report to the committee says peak debt reached £38.6m in October 2026. It recommends extending the Development Facility Agreement until July 2029 to allow for delays in final completions.

Upcoming meetings include the Climate Change Steering Group on 26 November, which will discuss district-wide emissions and the Climate Action Plan. The Audit Committee meets on 30 November to review procurement and internal audit reports. The Licensing Panel meets on 1 December to consider a Premises Licence application for Mermaidian Rye Tea Rooms in Rye. The Standards Committee also meets on 1 December, though the agenda is not yet published.

title: Bexhill hospital unit gets first portable ultrasound system in trust
text:
The Bexhill Irvine Unit has received a new SonoSite MT Ultrasound System, the first of its kind introduced within East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust. The portable device is designed to support specialist rehabilitation and injection services for patients with complex needs following a stroke, brain injury, or neurological diagnosis.

Rehabilitation Consultant Karen Poole said the technology allows for real-time imaging at the point of care. This ensures treatments, such as Botulinum Toxin injections for spasticity, are delivered with increased precision and safety. The compact design also supports complex cannulation and image-guided joint injections.

The trust said the investment helps reduce the need for patients to transfer to acute sites for these procedures. By keeping care local, the unit aims to improve treatment effectiveness and support best practice standards in musculoskeletal and rehabilitation care across East Sussex.

title: Battle Christmas events begin with fair and light switch-on
text:
Battle Town Council has published a schedule of festive events for the town, starting on Saturday 28 November. The day features a Taste of Sussex at Battle Abbey School, a Christmas Fair at St Mary’s Church, and Santa’s High Street Parade.

The festivities continue with Santa’s Grotton in the Memorial Hall, fairground rides on Abbey Green, and the Christmas Light Switch On at 5pm. On Sunday 29 November, St Mary’s Church hosts a Winter Wonderland Christmas Tree Festival.

Further events include late-night shopping on 3 and 11 December, a Christmas Market in Market Square, and a Tractor Run on 20 December. The council noted that free parking will be available on 28 November, 5 December, 12 December, and from 4pm on 11 December.

title: Bexhill zebra crossing relocated to improve safety
text:
A zebra crossing in Bexhill town centre has been relocated further south, the county council said. The move allows motorists to complete a full turn from Endwell Road before stopping at the crossing, improving safety for pedestrians.

East Sussex County Council lead member for transport and environment Cllr Peter Griffiths said the area is now safer for all road users. He noted the crossing is used by pupils walking to and from St Richard’s Catholic College.

Additional work on Sea Road included carriageway patching, footway reconstruction, and drainage improvements. New road markings and signage were installed to ensure the area is clearly laid out.

title: Tributes paid to Bexhill panto legend Ken Stevens
text:
Tributes have been paid to Kenneth Stevens, a well-known figure in Bexhill who died peacefully in his sleep on November 6, aged 90, at the Conquest Hospital. His niece, Kate, said he was a beloved local presence, often remembered for writing, performing in, and making costumes for pantomimes.

Mr Stevens grew up at 136 London Road, Bexhill, and attended the Bexhill Downs School for Boys. He was the brother of Eileen Stevens, who served as mayor of Bexhill three times and was the longest-serving magistrate in Sussex at the time of her death. Kate noted that his passing occurred exactly 25 years to the day after his sister’s death.

Beyond his theatrical work, Mr Stevens had a varied career, including roles as an air steward for British European Airways and a stallholder at Rye Market for 27 years selling antiques. He also operated shops in Bexhill and St Leonards, including an antique shop at 92 Bohemia Road and a fancy dress shop in King's Road.

title: Rother council reports 14 concluded conduct complaints
text:
Rother District Council’s Standards Committee is due to meet on Tuesday 1 December to review a six-monthly update on councillor conduct.

A report by the council’s Monitoring Officer, Philip Baker, states that 14 Code of Conduct complaints were concluded between June and November 2026. The report notes that the triage stage continues to reduce the resource burden of minor complaints.

One upheld case involved Councillor Connor Winter, following comments made in July 2025. An independent investigation found breaches of the Members' Code of Conduct. Councillor Winter agreed to a local resolution, which included a public-facing statement, written apologies, and refresher training on social media use. The committee supported this resolution in July 2026.

The committee will also review a report on Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman complaints. Mark Adams, Head of Digital and Customer Services, reported that four cases were determined in the period, with one regarding planning applications not investigated due to insufficient evidence of fault.

title: Person injured following two-vehicle collision on A259 between Eastbourne and Bexhill
text:
A two-vehicle collision involving a motorcycle and a car occurred just before 7.40am on Monday, 23 November, on the A259 between Eastbourne and Bexhill.

A spokesperson for Sussex Police said one of those involved sustained a minor injury. The accident caused long delays and congestion in both directions at the B2095 Hooe turn-off.

According to AA Traffic News, the congestion extended to the Pevensey Roundabout and over two miles back into Bexhill to Little Common.

title: On this day 1885: Maid of Kent rescue
text:
On 24 November 1885, the Rye lifeboat was called to the aid of the fishing smack Maid of Kent. This incident is recorded in the service history of the station, which operated from Camber Sands for 44 years before closing in 1901. The rescue was part of a long tradition of maritime assistance in the area, following earlier calls to vessels such as the steamship Medea in 1882 and the brigantine Cyrus in 1871.

The station, initially named Camber Lifeboat Station, was established in 1857 by the Royal National Lifeboat Institution. It was situated to the east of Camber Coastguard Station and to the west of the village of Camber, on the east bank of the River Rother estuary. Over the decades, the station received several new boats, including the Mary Stanford in 1881 and the Edward and Lucille in 1893. Coxswain James Collins was awarded the RNLI Silver Medal in 1891 for his gallant services, which included helping to save 45 lives over a period of 12 years.

Today, nothing remains of the boathouses at Camber Sands. The final lifeboat, the Edward and Lucille, was transferred to Scarborough and then St Annes, where she was wrecked while operating as a boarding boat.
